REAL ESTATE

30-Year Fixed: 7.51% +0.01  |  15-Year Fixed: 7.04% +0.01

More owners are carrying a mortgage into their late 70s. In 2025, 28.7% of U.S. homeowners 75 and older still had a mortgage, up from 20.3% in 2010, and their number more than doubled to about 3.9 million, according to Census Bureau survey data. In Alameda County the share is 41.5%, about 19,600 households, up from 27.3% in 2010 and above California's 39.1%.

Why it matters for supply. If more of those owners stay put, fewer homes come up for resale. An existing loan is paid off from the sale at closing, so on its own it is not a reason for any seller to wait. Buyers, resale supply stays thin when owners stay put, so be preapproved before the right home lists.

Rates. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average was 7.51% at Monday's update and the 15-year 7.04%; Tuesday's reading had not posted by 8:56 AM PT. On today's $1,275,000 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $7,139 a month in principal and interest.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,381 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,408 Monday, with 132 coming soon and 136 brand new. The five city ledger carries 604 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 539 on the market and 65 coming soon, down from 606.

Fremont holds 205 live listings: 166 active, 24 coming soon and 15 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,275,000 at $787 a square foot and a typical listing out 39 days. Hayward carries 176, Milpitas 96, Newark 70 and Union City 57. Across all five cities the median list price crossed a million, to $1,024,950 at $666 a square foot; 268 homes are priced under a million, and 191 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

STOCKS

S&P 500: 7,416.59 -1.92%  |  Dow: 51,608.17 -1.41%  |  Nasdaq: 24,509.76 -2.49%

Chips led a hard Monday. The Nasdaq closed down 2.49% at 24,509.76, the S&P 500 down 1.92% and the Dow down 1.41%, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index lost 5.28%. Fremont's Lam Research fell 6.68% and Milpitas's KLA 5.49%.

Nvidia reports tonight. Nvidia closed Monday at $156.14, down 4.12%, and reports quarterly results after the close today, its first since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. Market Briefs also reports that Anthropic, the San Francisco company behind Claude, is set to begin trading Thursday. Tuesday is lower again; at 8:56 AM PT the Dow was down 1.61%, the S&P 500 1.37% and the Nasdaq 1.48%.

ECONOMY

10-Year Treasury: 5.12% -0.03%  |  Gold: $3,853.00 -0.86%  |  Silver: $46.86 -4.60%  |  Brent Crude: $92.44 -3.55%

Diesel slipped under $6. The U.S. average was $5.94 in the Energy Information Administration's Nov. 16 survey, the first week under $6 since early September and down from the $6.53 record on Sept. 21. California is at $7.73, about $1.80 above the national average and off its own $8.25 record that week. Diesel is still up about 53% from a year ago, and it moves the trucks behind groceries and building materials alike, so a lasting slide would ease prices down the line.

Rates and metals. The 10-Year Treasury yield closed Monday at 5.12%, down from 5.15% Friday; Market Briefs printed it up at 5.13%. Gold settled at $3,853.00 and silver at $46.86, and both are firmer this morning: gold near $3,868.30 (+0.40%) and silver near $47.46 (+1.28%). Brent settled at $92.44, down 3.55%, not the $91.68 Market Briefs printed, and is near $93.27 this morning. The 10-Year is near 5.10%.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Bitcoin: $63,574 -1.62%  |  Ethereum: $1,773.73 -2.60%  |  XRP: $0.95 -0.15%

Bitcoin is still near its lows. Bitcoin is near $63,574, down 1.62% over the past 24 hours, live from CoinGecko at 8:56 AM PT, after sliding to about $62,600 over the weekend, its lowest since mid July. Ether is near $1,773.73 and XRP near $0.95. Strategy, the company with the biggest bitcoin holdings, fell 7.70% Monday and is down 5.42% this morning; Market Briefs reports that MSCI will drop it from its USA index after Nov. 30.
